# Programming / Backend & API Development

Design and build backends that hold up at very high scale: REST endpoints and OpenAPI specs with capacity planning to a million requests per second, versioning, pagination, errors, GraphQL and gRPC schemas and evolution, JWT, OAuth2/OIDC, cookies, RBAC, API keys and passkeys, Kafka, RabbitMQ, job queues, Celery, outbox and idempotency, Redis caching and connection pools, resilient third-party integrations, webhooks and Stripe, WebSockets and SSE, and serverless functions and workflows.

## REST API design

| Skill | What it does | Scripts |
|-------|--------------|---------|
| [rest-api-endpoint-designer](rest-api-endpoint-designer/SKILL.md) | Design REST endpoints that are correct for clients and hold up at extreme scale (hundreds of thousands to a million requests per second): resource modelling, URIs, methods and their safety and idempotency, request and response shapes, filtering, sorting, sparse fieldsets and expansion, bulk and batch endpoints, long-running operations (202 + status resource), conditional requests (ETag, If-None-Match, If-Match), caching headers for CDNs, compression, idempotency keys, rate-limit headers, and the scale architecture behind them: edge caching, regions and cells, stateless services, sharding by a key, hot keys, load shedding and retry budgets. Ships capacity_plan.py, which turns a peak request rate, latency, cache hit rates and payload sizes into CDN offload, per-region and per-cell traffic, instance counts with headroom, requests in flight (Little's law), database read/write load and bandwidth,. | `capacity_plan.py` |
| [openapi-spec-writer](openapi-spec-writer/SKILL.md) | Write and review OpenAPI 3.0 and 3.1 specifications that serve as the single contract for docs, SDKs, mocks, validation and tests: design-first workflow, document structure, reusable components (schemas, parameters, responses, security schemes), JSON Schema 2020-12 in 3.1, stable operationIds, tags, examples, problem+json errors, cursor pagination, idempotency and rate-limit headers, ETags, security schemes (OAuth2, bearer, API key), webhooks and callbacks, and the CI pipeline around the spec (Spectral rulesets, Prism mocks, contract tests, breaking-change checks, generated SDKs). Ships openapi_lint.py (JSON, or YAML with PyYAML) that resolves local refs and reports missing or duplicate operationIds, unresolved refs, path parameter mismatches, missing error responses and schemas, unbounded list responses and request fields, missing security, POSTs without Idempotency-Key, no 429s and missing examples. | `openapi_lint.py` |
| [rest-api-versioning-strategist](rest-api-versioning-strategist/SKILL.md) | Choose and run an API versioning strategy that lets the API evolve without breaking clients: what counts as a breaking change, evolving compatibly first (additive changes, tolerant readers, expand-and-contract), when a new version is justified, and the strategies with their trade-offs (URI major versions, header or media-type versions, date-based versions with per-account pinning and version transformers as Stripe does), plus deprecation and sunset policy (Deprecation and Sunset headers, timelines, usage telemetry, migration guides, brownouts). Ships openapi_diff.py, which compares two OpenAPI 3.x specs and classifies changes as breaking (removed operations or fields, type changes, new required inputs, tightened constraints, renamed operationIds), potentially breaking (new response enum values, properties becoming optional) or safe. | `openapi_diff.py` |
| [api-pagination-designer](api-pagination-designer/SKILL.md) | Design list endpoints that stay fast and correct at any depth and traffic: cursor (keyset) pagination as the default with opaque, versioned, tamper-proof cursors, stable ordering with a unique tiebreaker, matching composite indexes and row-value SQL, page size defaults and caps, total counts (avoid, approximate or separate), bidirectional paging, consistency under inserts and deletes, filters bound to cursors, sync endpoints with updated_after watermarks, Link headers (RFC 8288) and GraphQL Relay connections, plus pagination over shards, search engines (search_after with point-in-time) and caches. Explains why OFFSET pagination collapses at depth and scale and when it is still acceptable. | - |
| [http-status-code-advisor](http-status-code-advisor/SKILL.md) | Pick the correct HTTP status code for every API outcome according to RFC 9110 and related RFCs, and use status codes as the contract that clients, retries, caches, load balancers and SLOs depend on: 200/201/202/204 for success, 304 and conditional requests, redirects, 400 vs 422 for invalid input, 401 vs 403 vs 404 (and hiding existence), 405, 406, 409 vs 412 for conflicts, 410 for sunset resources, 413, 415, 428, 429 with Retry-After, 500 vs 502 vs 503 vs 504, which codes clients may retry, which are cacheable, and how codes feed error budgets and alerting. Reviews APIs for 200-with-error-body, 500 for client mistakes, 404 vs 403 leaks, wrong retry signals and codes that break caching. | - |
